title: Start a newsletter
pitch: Start a newsletter or blog from nothing.
opening: A few quick questions so your team knows you.
Pick a number or say it your own way. There are no wrong answers.

questions.line: Who do you want to write for?

choices.label: People in my line of work
choices.says: people in your line of work

choices.label: People who love what I love
choices.says: people who love what you love

choices.label: People in my town or city

questions.line: What do you know or love that they do not have yet?

choices.label: Lessons I learned the hard way
choices.says: the lessons you learned the hard way

choices.label: Good things I find before others do
choices.says: the good things you find first

choices.label: How I do my work, step by step
choices.says: how you do your work, step by step

choices.label: A craft or hobby I am deep into

questions.line: How do you want to sound?

choices.label: Like a friend passing on a tip
choices.says: like a friend passing on a tip

questions.line: How often can you really write? Pick the honest one.
A year from now, what would make you proud?

choices.label: A stranger says it helped them
choices.says: a stranger tells you it helped them

questions.line: What number would tell you this is working? Say it your way.
questions.hint: Not sure yet? Press enter. You can add it later.
Not sure yet? Press enter. You can add it later.

will: Show up {rhythm}, even when the issue is short.
will_not: Pretend to know what you do not. Say so and keep going.
Buy readers or message people who did not ask.
Send anything you did not approve.

your_part: You say when a sample sounds like you.
You press publish. Nothing goes out without you.
You decide if and when to charge.

team.name: editor
team.job: Turns your rough lines into issues that still sound like you.

team.name: researcher
team.job: Finds what your readers ask about and where they already gather.

team.name: growth
team.job: Finds your first readers and drafts ways to share that you approve.

team.name: publisher
team.job: Sets up where issues live and keeps your send days on the calendar.

chapters.title: Find your voice
chapters.finish_line: You approved one sample that sounds like you.
chapters.take: Write the way you talk. A voice you can keep up beats a polished one you cannot.

moves.you: Name your newsletter. Say three names out loud and keep the one that makes you smile.
moves.brief: Wait for the name. It is theirs to pick. If they ask for help, offer three names that fit {readers} and a voice {voice}, then let them choose.

moves.you: Write three rough sentences about one thing you wish you knew a year ago. Rough is the point.
moves.brief: Do not write these for them. When the three sentences arrive, save them as they are in {run_dir}/first-lines.md.

moves.you: Your editor turns your three sentences into a short sample in your voice.
moves.brief: Read {run_dir}/first-lines.md. Write a sample issue of about 150 words for {readers}, sounding {voice}. Keep their own words where you can. Save it as {run_dir}/voice-sample.md and say it is ready.

moves.you: Read the sample. If it sounds like you, approve it. If not, say one thing to change.
moves.brief: This call is theirs. If they ask for a change, make only that change and show the sample again.

chapters.title: First issue out
chapters.finish_line: Your first issue is live and you have the link.
chapters.take: Send it before it feels ready. Three hundred honest words beat a perfect issue that never goes out.

moves.you: Your publisher picks a free place for your issues to live and writes the five clicks to set it up.
moves.brief: Pick one free place to publish a newsletter. Write the setup as five short steps the person can do in under ten minutes. Do not make accounts for them. Save it as {run_dir}/where-it-lives.md.

moves.you: Your researcher gathers three things worth saying in issue one.
moves.brief: Find three things {readers} want to know that fit {gift}. One line each, with where you found it. Save as {run_dir}/issue-one-outline.md.

moves.you: Write issue one from the outline. Three hundred words is a real issue.
moves.brief: The writing is theirs. If they ask, the editor can tighten it, keeping their voice. Do not add new ideas.

moves.you: Press publish. Then keep the link as your proof.
moves.brief: Only they press publish. Once it is live, save the link in {run_dir}/issues.md.

chapters.title: First 10 readers who are not friends
chapters.finish_line: 10 people you did not know before signed up.
chapters.take: Go where your readers already talk. Ten strangers who chose you matter more than a hundred friends being kind.

moves.you: Your researcher finds five places where your readers already gather.
moves.brief: Find five public places where {readers} already talk: forums, groups, newsletters they read. One line each on why it fits. Save as {run_dir}/where-readers-are.md.

moves.you: Your growth seat drafts three ways to share issue one, in your voice, for you to pick from.
moves.brief: Write three short ways to share issue one in the places from where-readers-are.md, each sounding {voice}. Drafts only. Never post or message anyone. Save as {run_dir}/share-ideas.md.

moves.you: Pick one way to share and do it once today.
moves.brief: Only they share. Do not post for them.

moves.you: Count readers you did not know before. When you reach 10, write the count as your proof.
moves.brief: Keep a plain count of new readers who are not friends or family in {run_dir}/readers.md. Counts only, no names.
moves.proof_hint: how many and where you counted

chapters.title: A steady rhythm for four issues
chapters.finish_line: Four issues out on your rhythm, none skipped.
chapters.take: A short issue on the day you promised beats a long one a week late.

moves.you: Your publisher puts your next send days on the calendar, {rhythm}.
moves.brief: Plan the next three send days {rhythm}. Write them as dates in {run_dir}/send-days.md. Drafts only, nothing gets sent.

moves.you: Your researcher keeps ten ideas ready so you never start from a blank page.
moves.brief: Keep ten issue ideas for {readers}, one line each, in {run_dir}/ideas.md. Replace an idea once it is used.

moves.you: Send issues two, three and four on your rhythm. Keep the four links as your proof.
moves.brief: Only they press publish. After each send, add the link to {run_dir}/issues.md.

chapters.title: First paid reader
chapters.finish_line: One reader paid you and the money is real.
chapters.take: Ask once, plainly, with one price. A kind reply is not a payment.

moves.you: Your growth seat drafts one simple paid offer for you to say yes or no to.
moves.brief: Draft one paid offer: what readers get and one price. Leave the price for the person to set if they have not. Save as {run_dir}/paid-offer.md. Do not turn on payments.

moves.you: Read the offer. Keep it, change it or drop it.
moves.brief: This call is theirs. Change only what they ask.

moves.you: Turn on payments and tell your readers once. Your proof is the first real payment.
moves.brief: Only they turn on payments and tell readers. A kind reply is not a payment. Count it only when the money arrives.
moves.proof_hint: the first payment you can see
